content:
sam-cs: ACME (CS-4721) escalated — Dedicated pool dp-acme-07 saw sudden throughput collapse starting ~10:15 PST, lots of 429s and higher tail latency. Can eng-runtime triage?

alex-eng: Can you drop a couple request_ids and the pool id from their logs?

sam-cs: pool: dp-acme-07
request_ids: r-20260317-101520-aaa1, r-20260317-101842-bbb2

monitor-bot: ALERT dp-acme-07: 429_rate spike, tokens/sec p95 down ~46% @ 2026-03-17T17:18:23Z

maria-sre: Looking at node metrics — queue_depth on node-12/13 jumped right when customer reported. Prefill latency correlated.

ian-platform: Noted: config rollout at 09:58:02 UTC pushed batcher-config v3.4.1 to dp-* pools (per deploy history). Could be a config/regression.

deploy-bot: Deployment complete: batcher-config v3.4.1 -> rpool:d_pools (09:58:02 UTC)

alex-eng: Grabbed runtime traces for the request ids. Search for "batch_window" and "batch_fill_pct" lines — paste below from node-12 logs.

maria-sre: node-12 logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T17:15:20Z] req=r-20260317-101520-aaa1 batch_window=14ms batch_fill_pct=20 prefill_ms=48 service_ms=130 kv_hits=0
[2026-03-17T17:18:42Z] req=r-20260317-101842-bbb2 batch_window=11ms batch_fill_pct=17 prefill_ms=62 service_ms=95 kv_hits=0
```
small fill pct, lots of micro-batches, prefill gets no chance to coalesce.

alex-eng: Config in v3.4.1 reads as deployed:
```
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  quantum_tokens: 64
  min_fill_pct: 30
  prefill_timeout_ms: 8
```

alex-eng: Hypothesis: quantum_tokens (64) too big for ACME's short-request workload (~40 tokens/request). Many requests never reach quantum and are emitted early leading to many tiny batches -> scheduling overhead and lower effective throughput.

maria-sre: Metrics show ACME avg request tokens ~42. With quantum 64 we see fragmentation and median batch_size=1-2 during bursts. That explains p95 tokens/sec drop and the 429 cascade.

sam-cs: ACME confirms request pattern: short prompts (30-70 tokens) in bursts every 2-3s.

alex-eng: Repro suggestion: run a small generator at ~40 tokens, 50 QPS, verify packing and emergent batch sizes. Example quick test:
```
for i in `seq 1 500`; do curl -s -X POST https://api.internal/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"a"*40}' &
 sleep 0.02; done
```

maria-sre: Ran similar on a canary node with v3.4.1. Observed many singleton batches, batch_fill_pct ~18-22%, prefill_timeout expelled early.

ian-platform: Short-term mitigation: propose override for dp-acme-07 -> quantum_tokens=16, min_fill_pct=55, prefill_timeout_ms=16. That should make scheduler wait slightly longer and prefer grouping smaller requests.

alex-eng: Agree. Also consider lowering max_batch_tokens? Not necessary now. The key is matching quantum to typical request size.

deploy-bot: Canary apply: batcher-config v3.4.2 (overrides: quantum_tokens=16, min_fill_pct=55, prefill_timeout_ms=16) -> dp-acme-07 (start)

maria-sre: Canary metrics after ~90s: batch_fill_pct climbed to ~60%, median batch_size increased, p95 tokens/sec recovered ~+40%, 429s reduced to baseline.

sam-cs: Customer reports traffic normalized around 10:34 PST. They saw intermittent errors during the spike but are back to normal and appreciative.

alex-eng: Root cause writeup: v3.4.1 defaults were optimized for larger-token throughput (e.g., long completions). When applied to short-prompt heavy tenants, the quantum/min_fill combination caused fragmentation -> microbatches -> excess scheduler overhead and request queuing -> throttles.

ian-platform: Action items (owners):
- Roll v3.4.2 conservative defaults to affected dedicated pools (deploy-bot) -> immediate (ian-platform)
- Add adaptive rule: if avg_request_tokens < 128 then set quantum_tokens=16 and min_fill_pct>=50 (ian-platform)
- Alerting: add signal - if batch_fill_pct < 25% && p95_latency rises -> trigger auto-canary or pager (maria-sre)
- Runbook: add a short checklist to distinguish noisy neighbor vs batcher misconfig (how to read batch_fill_pct, quantum mismatch symptoms) (maria-sre)

sam-cs: Marking CS-4721: awaiting 24h observation before close. I'll update ACME and leave notes.

alex-eng: Thanks all. If any reoccurrence, drop logs and tag #eng-runtime + me.

monitor-bot: RECOVERY dp-acme-07: 429_rate returned to normal @ 2026-03-17T17:34:12Z
